newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - November 4.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - November 4.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi. Tel:3326806, 3326813, 3326849 Fax:+91-11-3351006
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
Indian Express
CONGRESS REBELS MAY SUPPORT OPPOSITION IN UTTAR PRADESH

The Uttar Pradesh (U.P.) unit of the Congress party is making frantic efforts to avert a split in its ranks. It has asked the party leadership to withdraw support to the United Front (UF) government. The UF blocked the Congress-Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) move to form the government in U.P. under BSP leader Mayawati. Consequently, the BSP was making efforts to form the government with the help of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). The U.P. Congress leadership was afraid that a section of its legislators could join the emerging BJP-BSP alliance as nobody was ready to face another election at this juncture.
The Times Of India
SECRET DEAL SUSPECTED BETWEEN CONGRESS CHIEF AND PREMIER

Congress president Sitaram Kesri's indecisiveness on the issue of withdrawing support to the United Front (UF) government has made the party restive. Despite the UF's cold shouldering of the Congress call to back Mayawati for the chief minister's post in Uttar Pradesh, Kesri has refused to withdraw support to the UF. Party circles feel a deal, struck between Kesri and Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, may be the reason for the party chief's silence on the issue. They suspect Kesri may be trying to save his loyalists from being charged in the ongoing scams by playing cool on the UF. The matter may be discussed in the next Congress Working Committee meeting on Monday.
The Economic Times
ITC GLOBAL DEAL LEGAL, SAYS CENTRAL BANK

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) has differed with the Enforcement Directorate over the alleged foreign exchange irregularities committed by ITC Global Holding. The RBI, expressing its view in a letter, said ITC Global Holding being an independent entity incorporated outside India would not need permission under the foreign exchange regulations for its commercial transactions abroad. ITC Global is a wholly-owned subsidiary of ITC, Singapore. This was also before the firm's deputy chairman observed that some of their transactions could be violating foreign exchange rules.
INSURANCE COVER ON DEPOSITS IN NBFCS

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) is considering an insurance cover on deposits by investors in non-banking finance companies and other recognised financial companies. The RBI is in talks with finance companies and associations about the various aspects of the proposed deposit insurance. To start with, an amount of 20,000 rupees on the investors' deposits would carry the insurance cover. This would be revised after a detailed study of the investment pattern of a variety of finance companies, said sources.
SANDOZ SHAREHOLDERS UNHAPPY WITH SHARE-SWAP RATIO

Indian shareholders of Sandoz (India) Ltd are unhappy with the terms of their company's merger with Hindustan Ciba-Geigy (HCG). They feel the proposed swap ratio of 17 Sandoz shares for 10 of HCG, and that too after the demerger of its speciality chemicals business, was in favour of HCG shareholders. This resentment was reflected in heavy selling and the consequent 39 percent crash in Sandoz stock in four trading sessions after merger terms were announced. The HCG scrip moved up 14 percent in the same period.
CRUDE SHORTFALL MAY SWELL IMPORT BILL

The likely shortfall crude oil production this year may be to the tune of 4.8 million tonnes. The petroleum ministry has scaled down this year's oil economy budget estimates from 35.65 million tonnes to 30.85 million tonnes. This is likely to cause a massive increase in the oil import bill to the tune of 28 billion rupees. The Prime Minister is reported to have asked the petroleum ministry to study the situation and find out ways to tackle the implications of the short fall in oil production on economy.
RESIST MULTILATERAL TRADE REGIMES: PM

Prime Minister H. D. Deve Gowda urged the developing countries to resist attempts to impose multilateral regimes in areas like investment and moves to raise new and unrelated issues in the agenda of the world trading organisation. Speaking at the sixth summit of the Group of 15 developing countries in Harare, Gowda called for another round of talks for a new generalised system of trade preferences in favour of the Third World nations. Gowda declared that India would resist attempts to compress the entire frame provided under the GATT talks.
CANADA LIFE AND TCFC PLAN 50:50 VENTURE

Twentieth Century Finance Corporation (TCFC) and the Canada Life Assurance Company have joined hands to set up a 50:50 joint venture (JV) insurance company. The authorised capital of the new company is two billion rupees. The initial paid-up capital will be one billion rupees. According to the TCFC chairman, the Asian Development Bank, IFC and Commonwealth Development Corporation were interested to invest in the JV company. The three institutions are expected to invest up to 35 percent of the equity of the company. The joint venture will carry out only life and general insurance business.
Financial Express
GDRS FALL MORE STEEPLY THAN INDIAN SHARES

Shares of Indian companies listed on foreign stock exchanges have fallen more steeply than their counterparts listed on Indian exchanges. The Skindia global depository receipts (GDR) index - an index on the price movement of 64 Indian GDRs listed abroad - slipped 15.80 percent to 60.23 percent on October 31 from 71.54 on August 1, 1996. However, the 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange Sensitive index slipped only 9.91 percent to 3,163.78 on October 31 from 3,511.63 on August 2, 1996. Sources said foreign investors seemed to be apprehensive about the political and economic conditions in India.
INDIA TO EXPLORE 'CALCRETE' URANIUM

India will become the third country in the world to explore 'Calcrete' type of uranium deposits with the atomic minerals division of the department atomic energy undertaking extensive exploration plans soon. Australia and Namibia are the other countries which have exploited such deposits. The potential areas which contained such deposits in the country are Rajasthan, Gujarat and western parts of Andhra Pradesh. The government plans to lay a thrust on exploration of such deposits in the near future. Given the high cost of Uranium, the low grade deposits which can be explored economically, may provide a resource base for the country's 20,000 mw nuclear power programme by 2020 AD.
AMERICAN EXPRESS' NEXUS WITH MAJOR FIRMS BARED

A central bank report on the American Express (Amex) Bank revealed the nexus between Amex and several corporates, including Reliance Industries, Videocon, and the Birlas' Indo-Gulf. Amex made several large accommodative deals with these firms by extending funds in the form of bridge loans against foreign currency deposits, breaching consortium guidelines and not calling for relevant papers. The deals violated central bank norms wherein there was no proper credit appraisal or monitoring of the end-use of funds.
Business Standard
CONSORTIUM LENDING TO BE EASED

Consortium lending norms may be liberalised further. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) governor said this would follow as soon as changes the monetary policy were put in place. The recently announced monetary policy had stipulated that the banks would frame guidelines for consortium lending on their own. The RBI chief hinted at action against banks which failed to provide 12 percent of their net bank credit to the export sector. The apex bank chief said the monetary policy was in tune with past policies and rejected the view that lack of credit the caused of the decline in industrial production. The dip in industrial growth was due to decline in electricity growth and mining, he argued.
CELLULAR LICENCES TO BECOME ASSIGNABLE

The department of telecommunication (DoT) would allow assignability of cellular telecom licences. Senior officials said DoT would allow cellular companies after they make a formal request. When assignability for basic service licences was allowed, it was implicit cellular operators would also be allowed the same feature, a DoT official said. But he clarified that DoT had not received a request for assignability from any of the cellular operators.
The Observer
U.S. TO INVEST' $500 M IN INDIA'S INSURANCE SECTOR

U.S. investment in the Indian insurance sector will be in the $400-$500 million range once the sector is opened up to private players. This was said by U.S. congressional research service Rawle's leading insurance economist O. King. He said given the investment opportunites in the country's insurance sector, the Indian government should not delay the opening up of this sector.
EXTERNAL AID UTILISATION UP

Quantum of aid utilised by externally-aided projects during the April-August period went up by 36-38 percent as compared to that in the previous corresponding period. The finance ministry, after its quarterly review of these projects, predicted a major improvement in the aid utilisation rate in the current fiscal. Improvement in the progress of externally-aided projects was shared by all sectors, including power and irrigation, sources said. News of improved aid utilisation came in the wake of the World Bank's warning that bank-aided projects that were not implemented in time, could be killed.
DAEWOO TO INVEST $20 BLN

South Korean giant Daewoo Electronics has drawn up plans to invest nearly $20 billion in India during the next five years. This was stated the corporation's executive vice-president Kwi-Hyen Nam during his recent visit to India. He was here to launch Daewoo's consumer electronic products through its joint venture company Daewoo Anchor Electronics. Daewoo would invest mostly for setting up facilities for manufacturing automobiles and auto-ancillary units. A sizeable part of the investment would be made in consumer electronics, Nam informed.
